messages:
noah: Quick UX check: in the scorecard weight editor I added a tiny slider to adjust importance per metric but it breaks keyboard nav and the regression timeline scrubber overlap on narrow widths. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/score-21686.png

maya: thanks for calling out. Is the slider focusable via keyboard? what happens with arrow keys?

noah: slider responds to arrows but focus jumps to the timeline when you press Tab after adjusting. I think DOM order places timeline next; expected: continue to next form control (save/cancel).

leah: we should enforce a logical DOM order for form controls first, then the scrubber. Also for small widths the timeline sits under the metric row and visually looks like it's part of the metric controls which confuses screen reader users.

samir: agree. Implementation note: put the scrubber in its own landmark region and give it aria-label="Regression timeline" and tabindex="0" so it can be reached intentionally, but keep it after the primary form actions in the DOM flow.

rong: accessibility nit: slider needs aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-label that include metric name, e.g., `aria-label="Weight for precision metric"`. Also announce percent changes with an `aria-live="polite"` region.

noah: good. For the microcopy inside the slider tooltip I used `Importance: 20%`  thoughts on phrasing?

maya: `Weight: 20%` feels more consistent with other places where we use `weight` for scoring. Keep tooltip short.

leah: also consider adding a small help icon with a short description: "Weight affects final score calculation; higher = more influence." Link to docs for formula.

noah: regarding the timeline: in mixed-width breakpoints the scrubber's grab handle overlays the right-side overflow menu. Users clicking the menu hit the handle instead.

samir: can we add a larger hit target for the menu and z-index it above handle? But careful: if we z-index menu above timeline it might intercept pointer events when timeline is active. Maybe hide handles when menu is open.

rong: keyboard-only users need to be able to scrub via keystrokes too. Provide `Home/End` to jump, ArrowLeft/Right steps, and `PageUp/PageDown` larger jumps. Add a visible focus ring for keyboard users.

leah: design tradeoff: do we show expanded context lines in regression diff by default or collapsed? Expanded is clearer but noisy. We considered `Show context: 3 | 5 | 10` selector. Thoughts?

maya: default to 3 to reduce noise, allow keyboard-accessible quick toggle `c` when the diff has focus (shortcut shown in tooltip). But keyboard shortcuts must be discoverable: add a ? keyboard help panel.

noah: for the scorecard preview we render small bars for each metric; accessibility bot flagged contrast for the bar on the compact bg. designbot: contrast 3.6:1 for bar vs bg.


designbot: Contrast Advisory: metric bar on compact card fails WCAG AA for small text. Recommend either darker fill (metric-600) or a 2px outline.

samir: we'll switch to metric-600 for now and re-run checks. Also, ensure that the bar has aria-role="img" with aria-label="precision: 0.78" for assistive tech summary.

noah: last thing: approval flow UI when adjusting weights should have an explicit save/preview step to avoid accidental score drift. Current autosave changes scores immediately which caused confusion during testing.

leah: agree. Let's switch to `Preview` then `Save weights` pattern. Preview updates the scorecard visualization client-side, Save commits and logs the commit message. Add a small toast: "Weights previewed (unsaved)" with an action to revert.

maya: copy suggestion for save confirm modal: title `Save scoring weights?` body `Saving will update historical scorecards that reference this weight set. This action is versioned and can be rolled back.` primary `Save weights` secondary `Cancel`

rong: confirmation modal must include focus management and indicate if update affects historical runs (yes/no count). Use `aria-describedby` to include the count detail.

noah: i'll update the figma frames and create two states: compact (mobile) and desktop with improved DOM ordering. pushing shortly. please drop any microcopy nits here before EOD. :mag_right:
